freeze_policy: The v0.5 benchmark objective, gates, train/validation/test split, upstream pins, and reported test metrics are frozen. Any later tuning belongs to a new benchmark/version and must not overwrite this evidence lane.

upstream_pins.pysensors_baseline: SSPOR + QR + Custom(exact shared training POD basis)

configuration.anti_leakage: POD, ROM and sensor ranking fit on train only; design/reconstruction-method selection uses validation only; final comparison uses untouched test only.

supported_claims: On this frozen OpenFOAM-13 cavity benchmark, using the declared cost model and untouched test set, ObservableFlow v0.5 Pareto-dominates the pinned PySensors SSPOR/QR baseline on declared acquisition cost, noiseless full-reference NRMSE, and 1%-noise full-reference NRMSE.
The selected ObservableFlow design uses 3 spatial channels and temporal depth 4 versus 8 static channels for the selected PySensors baseline.
Both methods fail the predeclared noiseless NRMSE <= 0.50 deployment gate on the final test set.
Full rank alone is not sufficient evidence of stable or deployment-quality reconstruction.
unsupported_claims: ObservableFlow is generally superior to PySensors.
ObservableFlow is generally superior to commercial sensor-placement or digital-twin products.
The benchmark establishes performance on turbulent, high-Reynolds-number, multi-geometry, physical-hardware, or industrial datasets.
The benchmark establishes a universal physical value for the temporal-depth cost coefficient 0.25.
The software or benchmark solves the continuum Navier-Stokes existence/smoothness problem.

next_phase.name: ObservableFlow v0.6
next_phase.minimum_evidence_goal: Multi-case, multi-regime external benchmarking without modifying the frozen v0.5 evidence lane.
